events.html:
Recurring pattern

Integrations & Connectors

There is repeated uncertainty about when to use a knowledge/ingestion connector versus a live tool connection, and what each one carries over.

Questions we keep hearing

  • When should we ingest data into a searchable store versus query the source system live?
  • Do connectors carry over the original access rules from the source, or not?
  • Which connectors are read-only, and which can write changes back?
  • How fresh is connected data, and how often does it sync?

The expectation underneath

People expect a clear decision rule for the two connection styles and explicit clarity on whether source permissions and freshness are preserved.

A way to make it clearer

Present a side-by-side of the two connection styles at the moment of setup — covering search quality, write access, permission inheritance, and sync freshness — so the right choice is obvious before data moves.

An aggregated pattern paraphrased across multiple conversations — not any single call.

events.html:
Recurring pattern

Permissions & Access

Teams are unsure how role-based access is modeled and where access should actually be enforced — inside the product, or in the systems it connects to.

Questions we keep hearing

  • How do we hide advanced configuration from everyday users while admins keep full control?
  • Should fine-grained permissions live in the platform, or in the underlying system being connected?
  • How do we keep sensitive environments locked down so no one can make changes through an unexpected path?
  • What can each role do by default, and how do we tailor that per team?

The expectation underneath

People expect one obvious place to reason about who can do what, with safe defaults and a clear boundary between platform-level and system-level control.

A way to make it clearer

Offer a single access overview that visualizes effective permissions per role, and state plainly which controls belong to the platform versus the connected system — with guided presets for the most common setups.

An aggregated pattern paraphrased across multiple conversations — not any single call.

Aggregated patterns · not individual feedback

The Confusion Map

What our customers are asking about the most during discovery calls.

Recurring Occasional Emerging
No theme in this window recurs across enough separate conversations to show safely.

What became clearer

Themes that came up less often in the most recent period than they used to — places where the fog seems to be lifting.

Cost & usage visibility

Questions about tracking spend and attributing usage per person or team come up less than they used to — the concept seems to be landing.

Availability of newer capabilities

Uncertainty about whether recently released features are ready to rely on has eased as they have settled into general use.

Observability basics

Fewer conversations start from scratch on how activity and metrics surface — the reporting story is increasingly understood up front.

Aggregated and paraphrased from multiple calls.

enhancement.prompt: Build me an app that shows what our customers are asking about most during discovery calls, pulling from call transcripts and highlighting recurring themes sorted by frequency.
enhancement.response: The Confusion Map is ready — it highlights what customers ask about most during discovery calls. The app shows each question as a card with the question text, frequency count, and a bar showing how common it is compared to the most frequent one. It pulls from the "Customer Confusions" data source, which has questions logged from real discovery calls and their frequency counts. Just click the "refresh" button or ask me to reload it when you add new questions. Use it to quickly spot patterns in what confuses your customers.
